title: Set Up: The Mystery Feely Bag

scenes.tts: Your skin is for feeling. Even when you cannot see, your hands tell you if something is rough or smooth, hard or soft, warm or cold. Touch is one of your five senses.

items.text: Rough or smooth, hard or soft, warm or cold
Touch is one of five senses

scenes.narration: Your skin is for feeling. Even when you cannot see, your hands tell you if something is rough or smooth, hard or soft, warm or cold. Touch is one of your five senses.

scenes.tts: You need a pillowcase and eight to ten objects with different textures. Keep a metal spoon, a wooden spoon, and a spoon from the fridge aside for later.
scenes.narration: You need a pillowcase and eight to ten objects with different textures. Keep a metal spoon, a wooden spoon, and a spoon from the fridge aside for later.

scenes.tts: Pack the bag yourself. Your child feels one object without looking and gives three describing words, then guesses. Later, add the metal and wooden spoons.
scenes.narration: Pack the bag yourself. Your child feels one object without looking and gives three describing words, then guesses. Later, add the metal and wooden spoons.

scenes.tts: Most children find the metal spoon feels colder, though both are at room temperature. A cold spoon can feel wet, so check it with a towel. Touch cannot tell colour. Only your eyes can.

items.text: Cold spoon can feel wet: check with a towel

scenes.narration: Most children find the metal spoon feels colder, though both are at room temperature. A cold spoon can feel wet, so check it with a towel. Touch cannot tell colour. Only your eyes can.

scenes.tts: Stay with your child and check every object. Use objects too big to fit inside a toilet paper tube. Nothing sharp, hot, frozen, breakable, or alive goes in the bag.

scenes.line: Touch finds shape, texture, warm and cold, but not colour.
